subject: MIRT identifiability - how to constrain average intercept to 0 and average slope to 1

messages.author: 0e91faa8ebe139b2
messages.subject: MIRT identifiability - how to constrain average intercept to 0 and average slope to 1
parts:
Hi Phil,

Following the approach in Matthias' paper (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11336-011-9202-z), I'd like to constrain the average slope to 1 and the average intercept to 0, thereby allowing me to freely estimate the means and variances of the latent variables. 

Is there a way to do this?


Thanks for all your help with this.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: MIRT identifiability - how to constrain average intercept to 0 and average slope to 1
parts:
On Fri, Jun 23, 2017 at 10:01 AM, Charlie_Rutgers <charles.i...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,

Following the approach in Matthias' paper (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11336-011-9202-z), I'd like to constrain the average slope to 1 and the average intercept to 0, thereby allowing me to freely estimate the means and variances of the latent variables. 

Is there a way to do this?

Yes, see here: https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/html/Three-Rasch.html. You'll just need to add a slope constraint, and change the itemtype from Rasch to 2PL.

My question is, if it's just for identification purposes is there any point? You could just use whatever is convenient/most stable in the software because the model fit shouldn't change....

Phil
Thanks for all your help with this.

Thanks for the link - this is great, I'll give it a go.

Re: your question, the purpose is to build a longitudinal IRT model to measure change. The Embretson-type 2PL model is arranged such that the first factor is the "main dimension" second factor is the "change" or "growth" dimension. In the paper, von Davier et al freely estimate the means and variance of the two dimensions and then compare across groups the means of the change dimensions. NB: I could be screwing this up, but I think that's the idea. 

As always, thanks for your help, and good luck with the move to GA.

Charlie
